---
title: "Slope charts"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8.8, fig.height = 4.4, dpi = 100,
  fig.retina = 2, dev = "ragg_png", out.width = "100%"
)
options(gglaplot2.font = "inter")
library(ggplot2)
library(gglaplot2)
gbp <- scales::label_dollar(prefix = "£", scale = 1e-3, suffix = "k")
```

A slope chart compares two points in time: one line per series, a marker and
a label at each end, and no value axis to speak of.

```{r slope, fig.height = 5}
ends <- gla_yearly[gla_yearly$year %in% c(2015, 2024), ]
ends$label <- paste0(ends$series, "  ", gbp(ends$average))

ggplot(ends, aes(year, average, colour = series)) +
  geom_gla_line() +
  geom_gla_endpoint(where = "start") +
  geom_gla_endpoint(where = "end") +
  geom_gla_endlabel(aes(label = label), where = "start", dx = -8, hjust = 1) +
  geom_gla_endlabel(aes(label = label), where = "end") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2015, 2024), expand = expansion(mult = 0.45), position = "top") +
  scale_colour_gla() +
  gla_labs(title = "Every variable fell between 2015 and 2024", subtitle = "Yearly average value (GBP)",
           source = "LDN Viz Tools demo data", x = NULL) +
  theme_gla(gridlines = "none", legend = "none") +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.line = element_blank())
```

## Interactive

`gla_plotly()` turns the finished chart into an interactive one through
plotly. A slope chart converts with its two dates along the top, the lines
and markers, and the labels at each end set off their points as the static
chart sets them.

```{r interactive, eval = requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE)}
gla_plotly(last_plot())
```
